{{Short description|American statistician}}
'''Cathryn S. Dippo''' is an American [[statistician]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nap.edu/read/11992/chapter/16|title=Appendix G:Biographical Sketches of Committee Members and Staff|via=nap.nationalacademies.org}}</ref> She became a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1989.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://cwstat.org/about/people/asa-fellows/|title=ASA Fellows|date=March 29, 2016|access-date=May 14, 2022|archive-date=October 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025075400/https://cwstat.org/about/people/asa-fellows/|url-status=dead}}</ref>  

==Education==
She obtained a Ph.D. in [[mathematical statistics]] from [[George Washington University]].<ref name="auto1"/>

==Work==
In the mid-1980s she began the [[National Science Foundation]]/[[American Statistical Association]]/[[Bureau of Labor Statistics|BLS]] Senior Research Fellow Program. In the late 1980s she began the BLS Behavioral Science Research Center. She retired as associate commissioner of the Office of Survey Methods Research at the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] in the first decade of the 2000s. While at the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] she also chaired the Current Population Survey Redesign and the FedStats R&D Working Group.<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1145/602421.602450|title=FedStats: the gateway to federal statistics|first=Cathryn|last=Dippo|date=January 1, 2003|journal=[[Communications of the ACM]]|volume=46|issue=1|pages=55|via=January 2003|doi=10.1145/602421.602450|s2cid=10732972 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

She also worked as a [[Scholarly peer review|referee]] for statistical journals.<ref name="auto1"/>

==Affiliations==
From 1985 to 1986 she was a chairperson of the [[methodology]] section of the [[Washington Statistical Society]] (WSS); the WSS is a chapter of the [[American Statistical Association]].
From 1986 to 1988 she was a representative-at-large of the WSS. In 1989 she became a [[List of fellows of the American Statistical Association|Fellow of the American Statistical Association]], which she also became a lifetime member of at some point.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2014/02/01/lifetimemembers2_14/|title=Recognizing the ASA's Lifetime Members &#124; Amstat News|date=February 1, 2014}}</ref><ref name="auto"/>  She served as president of the WSS from 1989 to 1990.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://washstat.org/documents/12book.pdf|title=Washington Statistical Society, Past and Present, 1896 to 2012}}</ref> She was a Curtis Jacobs Memorial Award Coordinator for the WSS, and on their Curtis Jacobs Memorial Committee, from 1991 to 1993. In 1991 she also received the WSS Presidents' Award as part of the [[American Statistical Association|ASA]]-150 Committee. From 1992 to 1993 she was on the WSS's Committee on [[American Statistical Association|ASA]] Fellows.<ref name="auto2"/> 

She also became a member of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]].<ref name="auto"/>
